title: Rust package docs scope
summary: This file is the package-local documentation policy for the Rust implementation. It does not define the shared public website, shared protocol docs, TypeScript docs, Python docs, or the GraphReFly blog.
rules: The language-neutral authority lives in ~/src/graphrefly.
The shared graphrefly.dev website shell and public documentation architecture are owned by ~/src/graphrefly under D563.
This repo owns Rust package documentation inputs, the package-local Starlight site at rs.graphrefly.dev, and package docs automation only.

title: Repository boundary
rules: ~/src/graphrefly owns shared public docs, guide records, public blog storage/rendering, protocol authority, and dashboard/control views.

~/src/graphrefly-rs owns rustdoc comments, crate README material, Rust examples, development docs, crate release notes, docs.rs output, the package-local website/ Starlight site, and Rust package-local docs checks.
This repo must not hand-maintain mirrors of shared docs, TypeScript docs, Python docs, public blog posts, or the internal dashboard.

title: Authority order
rules: Protocol rules come from ~/src/graphrefly/spec/rules.jsonl.
Design locks and sequencing come from ~/src/graphrefly/decisions/decisions.jsonl and ~/src/graphrefly/plan/*.jsonl.
Public Rust API docs come from rustdoc on exported crate items.
Package usage and development notes live in README.md and docs/*.md when they are Rust-specific.
Shared public concepts and package delegation live in ~/src/graphrefly guide records.

title: Automation policy
rules: Rust API docs should be mechanically reproducible from rustdoc.
scripts/generate-rustdoc-comments.py is the repeatable path for broad missing-doc comment generation; it parses rustdoc missing_docs diagnostics and preserves existing docs.
The website/ Starlight build must generate rustdoc mechanically and copy it into the package-local Pages artifact, not hand-maintain API mirrors.
docs.rs/rustdoc output is generated and must not be copied into ~/src/graphrefly by hand.
Rust examples should compile or be covered by tests when practical.
Package-local docs checks should fail on stale or broken examples once a generator/check exists.
Release notes are package-local unless a shared public docs record deliberately links to or summarizes them.

title: Public Rust surface docs
rules: Document public structs, enums, traits, functions, modules, and feature-gated surfaces with rustdoc when they are user-facing.
Examples must use current clean-slate APIs and must not reference the retired port model, actor model, structural Impl parity, or old cross-track ledger.
Protocol-adjacent docs must cite or review the governing rules in ~/src/graphrefly/spec/rules.jsonl.
If Rust docs and shared rules disagree, fix the docs or run spec-amend before changing behavior.

title: Package-local material
rules: Rust development notes, examples, crate-specific architecture notes, release material, and the rs.graphrefly.dev package-local site remain package-local.
Shared graphrefly.dev pages may link or delegate to Rust docs but must not copy rustdoc, examples, release notes, or generated package-site content into the shared site.
Retired port-model migration notes, frozen API snapshots, audit reports, flowcharts, and review reports are not kept in the active docs tree; use git history for archaeology.
